description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: DJ Moore (shoulder) has been diagnosed with an AC joint sprain and his status is day-to-day. A source said "He has a chance to play next week, but it's not a lock."
items.impact: Moore was injured while trying to catch a pass in the endzone, falling hard on his shoulder as a defensive back rolled over top of him. At first the injury looked serious, but he was able to sit up and walk off the field under his own power. More than likely Moore will miss at least a week, but if there's any silver lining, the Bills get a mini-bye here thanks to the Thursday night game. Once he returns he will go back to being a featured target in the Bills passing attack. But if he misses time, Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir will be the primary targets for Josh Allen, but don't sleep on Keon Coleman, who saw some sneaky good usage once, and even before, Moore was knocked out.
items.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) diagnosed with AC joint sprain, status day-to-day

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Alec Pierce was seen practicing on Friday.
items.impact: Pierce did not practice on Thursday. His return on Friday gives him a good chance to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Cedric Gray has pretty much done everything necessary to be cleared but hasn't been yet.
items.impact: Gray practiced in full again on Friday. He could be cleared by Saturday from the concussion protocol.
items.title: Cedric Gray remains in concussion protocol

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Cor'Dale Flott will not practice on Friday, but he's still expected to play on Sunday against the Eagles.
items.impact: Flott will not practice due to tightness. His status will still be worth monitoring on the official injury report.
items.title: Cor'Dale Flott will not practice Friday, expected to play Sunday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: John Simpson was seen at the start of practice on Friday.
items.impact: Simpson missed the last two days of practice with groin injury. His status will need to be monitored on the official injury report.
items.title: John Simpson (groin) seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Nico Collins was not seen at the start of practice on Friday.
items.impact: Collins will likely be ruled out when the injury report is officially released.
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) not seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Aaron Banks had a good practice on Thursday in pads but still isn't ready to say he'll play Sunday.
items.impact: Banks will be worth monitoring when the official injury report is released.
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) uncertain for Week 2

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Bobby Brown III was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.impact: Brown missed practice all week. He'll likely be ruled out for Week 2 when the injury report is released later in the afternoon.
items.title: Bobby Brown III (back) not practicing Friday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: B.J. Hill (achilles) did not dress for Friday's practice session.
items.impact: Hill was on the sidelines with a noticeable limp Friday morning. The veteran defensive lineman seems like a long shot for Sunday's game.
items.title: B.J. Hill (achilles) not in uniform at Friday's practice

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Javon Kinlaw was back practicing on Friday.
items.impact: Kinlaw did not practice on Thursday. He should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.title: Javon Kinlaw (back) returns to practice Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Frankie Luvu was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.impact: Luvu did not practice on Thursday. He'll likely be ruled out when the injury report is officially released.
items.title: Frankie Luvu (groin) not practicing Friday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Samaje Perine (illness) was on the sideline at the start of Friday's practice session.
items.impact: Perine has missed Thursday's practice as well due to an illness. The veteran back was a significant part of the Bengals' offense in Week 1, rushing for 20 yards on five carries and grabbing three passes for 30 yards. Perine still has a couple of days to get ready for Sunday's matchup with the Texans.
items.title: Samaje Perine (illness) on the sidelines Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Chig Okonkwo was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.impact: Okonkwo did not practice last week. He should be ruled out when the official injury report is released.
items.title: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) not seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn confirmed that Jason Sanders will kick for the team in Week 2 against the Packers.
items.impact: Sanders connected on 3-of-4 field goals and 2-of-2 extra points in the Jets Week 1 win over the Titans.
items.title: Jason Sanders to remain Jets kicker in Week 2

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Michael Pittman Jr. was not seen to start practice on Friday.
items.impact: Pittman did not practice on Thursday. His status is uncertain for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) not seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Jalen Coker took part in special teams drills to begin practice on Friday.
items.impact: Coker was limited in practice to begin the week. He appears on track to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
items.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) takes part in special teams drills to begin practice

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Joe Burrow was seen stretching at the start of practice on Friday.
items.impact: Burrow was limited in practice on Thursday. He appears on track to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Texans.
items.title: Joe Burrow (back) seen practicing Friday

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Kyler Murray continues to progress through concussion protocol.
items.impact: Graziano notes that Murray did more in practice on Thursday than Wednesday. Once he is cleared, the Vikings will decide whether to start him on Sunday or play it safe by holding him out a week.
items.title: Kyler Murray progressing through concussion protocol

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Darnell Washington (personal) returned to practice on Friday.
items.impact: Washington missed Wednesday's and Thursday's practice session for personal reasons, but the big TE was back Friday. Washington secured both of his targets for 18 yards in Week 1's win over the Falcons.
items.title: Darnell Washington (personal) back at practice Friday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been practicing in full this week and will be ready for Sunday's game.
items.impact: Henderson was unable to go in Week 1, leaving the bulk of the backfield load to veteran Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson is in his second NFL season after totaling over 1,100 yards of offense and 10 touchdowns across 17 regular-season games as a rookie.
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ready for season debut

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: D'Angelo Ponds (calf) will play Sunday against the Packers.
items.impact: A second-round pick pick in this year's NFL Draft, Ponds was forced to put off his debut for a week due to a calf injury. The former Indiana Hoosier will be ready to take the field for the Jets in Week 2.
items.title: D'Angelo Ponds (calf) to debut Sunday

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Will McDonald IV (ankle) is expected to be ready for Sunday's game against the Packers.
items.impact: McDonald popped up on Thursday's injury report with an ankle issue, but the fourth-year pass rusher will be ready to go Sunday, according to head coach Aaron Glenn. McDonald picked up his first sack of the season in Week 1.
items.title: Will McDonald IV (ankle) good to go for Week 2

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: The Lions' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 41 points in Thursday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Detroit's defense looked terrible on Thursday night. They allowed Buffalo's offense to move the ball at will and gave up 41 points over the course of the night, which led to a loss for the team. They also looked poor against the Saints in Week 1, so this is shaping up to be a bad unit for the Lions, although we may get to see a better side to them with an easy schedule coming up over the next few weeks.
items.title: Lions D/ST dismal in loss Thursday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jake Bates went 4-for-4 on his extra-point attempts and made his lone field-goal attempt in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Bates did his job on Thursday night. He made all five of his kicks over the course of the game, so he carries no blame for Detroit's loss to the Bills. He should continue to be a quality fantasy asset at the position moving forward.
items.title: Jake Bates perfect in loss Thursday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Sam LaPorta hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: LaPorta had a good showing on Thursday night. He caught all but one of his targets and turned that into 52 yards and a touchdown in a shootout loss against the Buffalo Bills. He might struggle with consistency moving forward but will continue to have as high of a TD upside as anyone for the foreseeable future.
items.title: Sam LaPorta hauls in touchdown Thursday
